devin: quick q — thinking through admission-proxy (sidecar-per-pool) vs delegate autoscaler (central planner issues scale ops) for dedicated GPU pools. TL;DR: which pattern best preserves tenant SLOs + burst-credit semantics while keeping operator surface small?
sarah: short answer: hybrid is promising. Sidecars are great for low-latency admits and local KV cache ownership, but they multiply state and sync complexity. Central planner has global view for packing/cost.
max: FWIW we saw oscillations in the sim when local agents reacted to transient spikes. Sidecars without dampening = churn.
devin: pasted sim snippet:```bash
$ ./sim --scenario tenant-spike --trace=quick
[time=12s] tenant-A request spike -> sidecar admits 120 tokens
[time=13s] sidecar scales node -> central reconciler scales up 1 pod
[time=13.5s] another spike -> sidecar double-admits -> preempt pressure
```
rachel: hybrid idea: central planner issues medium-term reservations & budget caps; sidecar handles microburst admission up to a local allowance. Keeps fast path local, slow path global.
sarah: +tradeoffs: hybrid needs a clear contract: (1) how long reservations last, (2) how sidecar uses local allowance, (3) what visibility central has into sidecar consumption.
max: ops note: sidecars increase cardinality of logs/metrics. We should standardize an admit telemetry envelope to avoid noise. e.g., `admit{tenant,amount,reason,source}` as single-line JSON log.
devin: proto sketch for admission API (very small):
```proto
service Admission {
  rpc TryAdmit(AdmitRequest) returns (AdmitResponse);
  rpc Release(ReleaseRequest) returns (ReleaseAck);
}
message AdmitRequest { string tenant = 1; int32 tokens = 2; string trace_id = 3; }
```
orch-bot: canary metrics: hybrid prototype reduced 95p latency by ~6% in our test, and reduced unnecessary scale-ups in steady state.
rachel: failure modes: if sidecar crashes we must have central be able to step in (circuit-breaker fallback). Also need idempotency so replays don't double-count credits.
sarah: agreed. add these to RFC: fallback path + idempotency token + reconciliation job every N seconds.
max: one more: slot accounting. central has authoritative ledger for reservations; sidecar keeps ephemeral counters and periodically flushes/deltas. That keeps global correctness without synchronous RPCs on every request.
devin: propose next steps: 1) I'll open an RFC outlining hybrid contract + proto + reconciliation cadence, 2) prototype sidecar admit shim (no scaling decisions, just admit/release), 3) central planner that converts reservations to scale intents. Anyone want to co-author?
sarah: I can take the reconciliation and failure-mode section.
max: I'll own observability + sim regressions.
rachel: I'll add the test matrix (chaotic restarts, delayed reconciliation, simultaneous multi-tenant spikes).
devin: awesome. I'll ping infra to reserve a small canary pool once RFC lands. Thanks all :thumbsup:
